title: Generation of Inexpensive, Highly Labeled Probes for Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH)
protocol: Put 50 ng of purified template DNA in a final volume of 2 μl in an eppendorf tube.
Denature the DNA at 95°C for 3 min and immediately chill on ice for 5 min.
Add reagents to the denatured DNA in the following order: [Note: Specific reagent details not provided, use master mix for multiple tubes if applicable]
Mix 3 μl of nucleotide mixture with all nucleotides including amino-dUTP.
Add an additional 3 μl of nuclease-free water to achieve a total volume of 18.4 μl.
Vortex briefly and spin the tube.
Incubate the tube at 30°C for 12-16 hours.
Immediately proceed to heat inactivate the enzyme after incubation.
Heat inactivate the enzyme at 65°C for 10 minutes.
Cool the tube on ice.
Run 1-2 μl of the reaction on a 1% agarose gel.
Pool 100 ng of each template for amplification together.
Calculate the concentration (ng/ul) of the new master mix of fosmids if more than 10 templates are used simultaneously.
Take a volume corresponding to 50 ng of this new mix in a separate tube and amplify using the protocol above.
Add 370 ul of MilliQ water to the amplification reaction.
Place the sample in an ice box for sonication using a Branson sonifier.
Set the amplitude to 10%.
Sonicate the sample for 80 seconds.
Set the pulse time to 0.5 seconds (ON and OFF).
Purify the reaction using a PCR clean up kit or SPRI beads (1.8x Ampure) according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Elute in 80 ul MilliQ water.
Estimate the DNA concentration using Nanodrop.
Add purified glycogen as a carrier to the reaction for DNA precipitation.
Vortex and spin briefly, then incubate the reaction at −20°C for at least 1 hour.
Spin the tube at 16000 g for 12 minutes at 4°C.
Remove supernatant and wash pellet with 500 μl of 70% ethanol.
Spin again at 16000 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Air dry the pellet.
Add 6 μl of nuclease-free water to the tube and incubate at 37°C for 15 minutes.
Pipette gently to dissolve the pellet.
Denature the DNA by incubating the tube at 95°C for 3 min and immediately cool on ice.
Spin briefly and add fluorescent dye to the DNA fragments.
Vortex for 15 s, spin briefly and incubate at 18-24°C in the dark for at least one hour.
Purify DNA fragments coupled with fluorescent dyes.
Remove excess dye from purified DNA fragments.
Precipitate individual or pooled DNA fragments as needed.
Add 340 μl of MilliQ water to the reaction mixture.
Purify using a PCR purification kit or SPRI beads (1.8x Ampure).
Elute in 20 μl of MilliQ water.
Check probe concentration and absorption at specific wavelengths using Nanodrop's microarray function.
Transfer a volume corresponding to 400 ng of DNA of each probe into a separate tube.
Add components for precipitation and vortex vigorously.
Incubate the reaction at −20°C for at least 2 h.
Spin the reaction at 11,000 rpm for 20 min at 4°C.
Decant the supernatant and wash with cold 70% ethanol.
Spin for 5 min under the same conditions.
Remove the supernatant carefully and dry the pellet in the dark.
Dissolve the obtained pellet in 20 μl deionised formamide.
Store the dissolved probe at −20°C indefinitely.
Reconstitute probes in nuclease-free water if necessary before mixing different concentrations.
Add deionized formamide to the hybridization mixture for optimal FISH experiments.
